facts.fact: 她睡足了醒来；今早没有影子来传唤她，城堡白日里也空荡安静，仿佛昨夜什么都没发生。她骂出的那个名字是 Rabb——本章第一次出现国王的名字。
facts.anchor: I woke up refreshed and well-rested. There were no shadows to summon me this morning. Daylight flooded my empty chambers. Quiet. Still. As if nothing had even happened last night. Goddammit, Rabb.

facts.fact: 她手里握着昨夜留下的那枚发夹；她据此确认，即便昨夜对他毫无意义，那也毕竟是不可否认的证据。
facts.anchor: I studied the gleaming hairclip in my hand for a moment. Hope whispered in my heart once again. Even if last night meant absolutely nothing to him, it was confirmation—finally. It was undeniable proof.

facts.fact: 她由此得出结论：Rabb 记起了登基前的人生，记起了曾与她在一起，记起了“我们”。
facts.anchor: Rabb did remember. He remembered his life before he was crowned king. He remembered having been with me. He remembered us.

facts.fact: 她的推想：是不是有谁在逼 Rabb 装成怪物，或他正在拼命抵抗另一种咒。
facts.anchor: The next conundrum to tackle being then—why was Rabb acting this way? Was my theory correct? Was something or someone simply compelling him to act like a monster? Was he desperately trying to fight off another evil spell?

facts.fact: 墙上挂着旧金框的画像：国王、王后与年幼王子盛装含笑；她越看越觉得光不对，那欢乐被一层看不见的、从时间里倒着爬回来的悲伤盖住。
facts.anchor: One particular worn, gilded frame cradled a portrait of a king, a queen, and their young prince, all dressed in their finery, their smiles serene and untouched. But the longer I looked, the more the light seemed wrong, their joy dimmed by an unseen grief creeping backward through time, staining the image with the memory of what was to come.

facts.fact: 西翼那间荒屋：碎家具、撕破的帷幔、墙上的爪痕，一盏孤灯；The Wicked King 背对门站着，一只手揪住囚犯的衣领把人提到半空、靴子离地几寸。老人满脸尘土淤伤、嘴角带血地求饶“Mercy”，他回：整个王国都该早知道自己没有怜悯。
facts.anchor: The air was thick with the stale, dusty scent of neglect amidst the cold stone of the room. Broken furniture lay strewn like forgotten bones beneath torn drapery and claw-scarred walls. Candlesticks, brassware, weapons, and leather were scattered across a wooden table, with one lone lantern casting uneven light across the space. The Wicked King stood with his back partially to the door, tall and rigid, his dark coat almost blending into the sweep of shadows at his feet. A man hung in his grip. Literally. He had the man by the collar of his ragged tunic, one hand fisted in the fabric at his throat, lifting him so high that his boots dangled several inches above the floor. The elderly man’s hair was streaked with grey and plastered damply against his forehead. Dirt and bruises marked his face. Blood darkened the corner of his mouth, even as he whimpered, “Please—please, Your Majesty. I beg of you. Mercy.” The king’s retort was mocking. “Mercy? Hasn’t the entire kingdom learned yet that I possess no such thing?”

facts.fact: 囚犯临死诅咒他们是王国土里的杂草，拔了烧了撒盐也还会回来，并要“你和你那个女巫”付出代价；国王只答一声“Perhaps”，手指收紧后松手，影子像低语的黑刃割开他，血肉块块落地。
facts.anchor: The man’s livid eyes sharpened for a moment. He gave a hacking cough. “This will not end with me. We are the weeds in your kingdom’s soil—tear us out, burn us, salt the earth, and still we will return, rooting ourselves in cracks you cannot see. We will make sure you and your witch pay for everything you have done.” He tilted his head slightly, studying him with a cold, thoughtful expression. “Perhaps.” His fingers tightened. The man’s breath hitched as the king lifted him a little higher, his boots kicking uselessly in the air. Then he released his grip. A puppet with its strings cut. The man barely had time to suck in a breath before the entire room flooded with darkness for the blink of an eye. The Wicked King’s shadows, like swift whispering blades, ripped through the man, followed by dull thumps as hunks of flesh fell to the floor.

facts.fact: 树上暗处扑下一个人捂住她的嘴、粗布罩住她的头，喊声被闷住；她挣不过对方，被扛上肩，穿过森林带进树影深处。
facts.anchor: The words barely registered before something coarse dropped over my head. Darkness swallowed everything. I tried to scream, but it came out strangled, stifled by the thick fabric. I twisted and kicked, trying to wrench free, but the man holding me was stronger. The ground vanished beneath my feet as he hoisted me over his shoulder. The world lurched violently as he began moving. Branches slapped against my legs as he pushed through the forest, heavy thuds pounding against the ground with determined strides, even as his grip tightened to carry me deeper into the shadows between the trees.
